deviations.justification: fix-issue is a named lint source (zero literal tool binaries) and host.yaml has no issue-read capability (only change-request-*), so reading the issue body is stated as intent without a literal `gh issue view`.

Reads of repository state (current branch, default branch, repo toplevel, remote URL, branch existence) are reworded to state their intent without a literal git command because no workflow.* capability exposes them; for the backend/remote the TRD-039 resolver detection (`toolchain-cli explain`/`resolve`) is the source.

Plain git operations are workflow.* capabilities of the default `plain-git` workflow adapter (branch creation is `git switch -c` via workflow.branch-create, `git switch` already in the sequence); `git checkout -b` and `git town ...` are the non-default git-town path, not part of the unconfigured sequence.

No workflow.* capability stages files (plain-git workflow.commit is `git commit -m` only), so the source now states the staging intent ("stage exactly that path") without a literal `git add`; the agent still stages the same explicit paths before workflow.commit.
Branch creation (`git checkout -b` after a `git branch --list` check) is now workflow.branch-create whose default plain-git template is `git switch -c`.
The pre-refactor body instructed the commit in prose (`git add` then "commit") with no literal `git commit`; the refactor calls workflow.commit, whose default plain-git template is `git commit -m`.
The pre-refactor body pushed with prose/inline `git push -u origin` outside the scanned steps (not recognised as a step); the refactor calls workflow.push (plain-git default `git push`).
